subject: Reserved capacity scenarios and GPU-price sensitivity — BrightEdge
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity scenarios and GPU-price sensitivity — BrightEdge

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our call, I attached two capacity scenarios that map to the usage profile you shared: a 12-month conservative commit and a 24-month aggressive commit. Each tab shows SKU mix (A100x4, H100x2 equivalents), expected token throughput, and an estimated monthly invoice at current GPU-cost assumptions.

Key callouts:
- 12-month: 25% lower upfront discount but gives BrightEdge flexibility to re-evaluate mid-year; lower financial commitment if market GPU prices drop.
- 24-month: meaningful list-price discount (we modeled step tiers at 12/18/24 months) but increased exposure if GPU replacement/price deflation occurs.

From our side, the biggest lever is average GPU hour pricing (we modeled a +/−20% swing). For the 24-month plan, we can offer a larger committed-discount but will likely need an approval path for discounts >18% off list. If you can confirm which term you prefer and the internal approval timeline, I’ll get Karthik to prepare a formal commercial with the approval checkpoints and an estimated timeline for exec sign-off.

Attachments: BrightEdge-RFP-capacity-scenarios.xlsx, proposal-v3.pdf

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com

Sofia,

Appreciate the scenarios. Procurement will need a clear view on: 1) max downside exposure if GPU prices fall 20%, 2) what cadence for true-ups looks like, and 3) if there are mid-term opt-outs for material changes. Also, curious which pricing bands trigger the need for Redwood exec approval. Our legal team will want the commercial clean before procurement schedules a PO.

Can Karthik loop in finance on your side? We’re targetting a board review on Feb 2.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@brightedge.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity scenarios and GPU-price sensitivity — BrightEdge

Hi Maria — quick note from an infra perspective:

- The SKU mix in tab B (H100-heavy) reduces per-token latency for the rerank path but increases cost per GPU-hour by ~12% in our model. If you prioritize peak latency we recommend mixing H100 for inference-critical endpoints and A100s for bulk embedding/async jobs.
- For the true-up cadence: monthly reconciliations with a quarterly capped true-up window is standard for our Reserved Capacity customers. We can also add a mid-term rebalancing clause (once per 12 months) to change a % of the SKU mix without penalty.

If you share a target SLA or p95 latency threshold for the critical route, I’ll sketch a recommended SKU allocation.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@brightedge.ai, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@brightedge.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity scenarios and GPU-price sensitivity — BrightEdge

Maria / Procurement,

Thanks for the clarity. To address the approval/discount question: our commercial grid allows up to 15% off list for standard AE approvals; anything above 15–25% requires a finance review, and discounts >25% require VP/Revenue Ops sign-off. Evelyn — can you confirm the current band thresholds and whether we have latitude to bridge to 20% for strategic early customers like BrightEdge?

On the contract mechanics: we can include a price-protection addendum that adjusts unit list prices if our underlying GPU procurement cost changes materially, with a mutual review trigger at 12 months. That would limit BrightEdge downside exposure while protecting Redwood vs supplier-cost inflation.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity scenarios and GPU-price sensitivity — BrightEdge

Karthik / team,

Quick finance read: current delegated discount authority is: AE up to 15%; Finance review needed 15–25% with scenario P&L and downside stress tests; >25% requires VP+ sign-off and a commercial recovery plan. For this account, a 20% blended discount across a 24-month commit is plausible if: 1) BrightEdge signs a minimum monthly commit floor, 2) we include a 12-month price-protection clause with a defined audit/true-up, and 3) we get a preliminary procurement PO before Feb 5 (so the revenue can be modelled into Q1).

Evelyn
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

We reviewed the commercial terms. Legal is comfortable moving forward with a 24-month commitment that includes: a monthly commit floor, a price-protection addendum (mutual review trigger at month 12), and an annual true-up mechanism capped at a 10% quarterly adjustment. We will push standard limited termination rights tied to vendor price-shock (e.g., supplier hardware price drop >30%) rather than a broad opt-out.
